subject: Order Form - Limitation of Liability cap: proposal and specific questions
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@aurorahealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@aurorahealth.com, David Bennett <david.bennett@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form - liability cap proposal

Hi Dev,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal reviewed the draft Order Form and have a couple of open items around the limitation of liability. High-level ask from our side:

- Can we get the cap tied to "fees paid in the twelve months prior to the claim" rather than a multiple of annual fees? Aurora prefers a rolling-12 approach for budgeting.
- We need to preserve carve-outs for breach of confidentiality and IP indemnity. Also want clarification on whether consequential damages are excluded for both parties.

I've attached a marked-up Order Form with our suggested replacements (Attachment: Aurora_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.docx (docx)). I can also share a short model showing cap impact on our projected spend (Attachment: Liability_Cap_Modeling.xlsx (xlsx)).

Can you put together Redwood's preferred positions and any compromise language you can live with?

Best,

Sarah Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurora Healthtech

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form - liability cap proposal

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear notes and the redline. Quick summary of Redwood's current position and where we can compromise:

1) Baseline cap: Our standard is 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months (rolling-12) OR total fees paid under the agreement (contract term). We're open to either but need clarity on auditability and accounting alignment.
2) Multiples vs absolute: For customers with predictable annual spend, a multiple provides a deterministic ceiling. For customers with lumpy purchasing, a rolling-12 ties closer to recent consumption and reduces tail risk.
3) Carve-outs: Redwood will agree to standard carve-outs for breach of confidentiality, willful misconduct (where permitted), and IP infringement indemnities. We typically exclude consequential, incidental, and punitive damages for both parties.

Questions for Aurora:
- Do you have a preference between "rolling 12" (fees in prior 12 months) vs "annualized" (fees in a calendar/fiscal year)?
- If we propose 2x rolling-12, are you materially different than 1x rolling-12?

Looping in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (sales ops) to synthesize language we can send back.

Thanks,

—Dev
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@aurorahealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form - liability cap proposal

Sarah / team —

Thanks for the redlines. I've reviewed the doc and drafted compromise text inline (see attached). Key points we propose:

- Proposed cap: "Aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) $1,000,000; or (b) an amount equal to two (2) times the Fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim."
- If Aurora prefers a single-year absolute figure instead of a multiple we can consider a flat cap tied to committed annual spend, but that requires an explicit Order Form commitment and typically moves negotiations to commercial.
- Carve-outs: We accept carve-outs for (i) breach of confidentiality, (ii) gross negligence/willful misconduct (subject to CEO sign-off if requested), and (iii) Redwood's indemnity obligations for IP infringement. Consequential damages remain excluded for both parties; we can retain limited indirect damage carve-outs for loss of data where we have demonstrable fault.

Attachment: Aurora_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.docx (redlines with proposed language)

Next steps: Dev / Karthik — can you confirm whether Aurora has committed annual spend in the order (if yes, we can present the flat cap variant) or if they want the rolling-12 standard? Sarah — if you can confirm, we'll issue a clean tracked-change clause for sign-off.

Regards,

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form - liability cap proposal

Sarah — quick follow-up from procurement ops perspective.

We looked at Aurora's forecast and there is no firm committed spend in the Order Form (it's usage-based). Given that, Redwood's preference is rolling-12 to reflect actual consumption. From Aurora's standpoint, if 2x rolling-12 is a concern, we could do 1x rolling-12 with an underwriting review and a short-term credit hold provision.

If you could confirm whether Aurora would accept either (a) 2x rolling-12 or (b) 1x rolling-12 + underwriting, we can get legal to send the updated clause today.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
